### CVE-2026-3102 — exiftool PNG File MacOS.pm SetMacOSTags os command injection
- Assigner: VulDB | Published: 2026-02-24 | Updated: 2026-02-27 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: CWE-78 OS Command Injection; CWE-77 Command Injection
- CVSS 4.0 (cna): 5.3 MEDIUM `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:P/VC:L/VI:L/VA:L/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N/E:P`
- CVSS 3.1 (cna): 6.3 MEDIUM `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L/E:P/RL:O/RC:C`
- CVSS 3.0 (cna): 6.3 MEDIUM `CVSS:3.0/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:L/I:L/A:L/E:P/RL:O/RC:C`
- CVSS 2.0 (cna): 7.5 None `AV:N/AC:L/Au:N/C:P/I:P/A:P/E:POC/RL:OF/RC:C`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

A vulnerability was determined in exiftool up to 13.49 on macOS. This issue affects the function SetMacOSTags of the file lib/Image/ExifTool/MacOS.pm of the component PNG File Parser. This manipulation of the argument DateTimeOriginal causes os command injection. The attack is possible to be carried out remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. Upgrading to version 13.50 is capable of addressing this issue. Patch name: e9609a9bcc0d32bd252a709a562fb822d6dd86f7. Upgrading the affected component is recommended.

Affected:
- n/a / exiftool: affected 13.0; affected 13.1; affected 13.2; affected 13.3; affected 13.4; affected 13.5; affected 13.6; affected 13.7; affected 13.8; affected 13.9; affected 13.10; affected 13.11; affected 13.12; affected 13.13; affected 13.14 …(+36 more in JSONL)

Credits: owl4444 (VulDB User)

### CVE-2026-20613
- Assigner: apple | Published: 2026-01-22 | Updated: 2026-01-23 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: The ArchiveReader.extractContents() function used by cctl image load and container image load performs no pathname validation before extracting an archive member. This means that a carelessly or maliciously constructed archive can extract a file into any user-writable location on the system using relative pathnames.; CWE-22 CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

The ArchiveReader.extractContents() function used by cctl image load and container image load performs no pathname validation before extracting an archive member. This means that a carelessly or maliciously constructed archive can extract a file into any user-writable location on the system using relative pathnames. This issue is addressed in container 0.8.0 and containerization 0.21.0.

Affected:
- Apple / Container: affected unspecified <0.7.1 (custom)
- Apple / Containerization: affected unspecified <0.20.1 (custom)

- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.7 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=partial

NIOSSLCertificate._subjectAlternativeNames provides access to the raw bytes for a cert's SANs. NIOSSL provides access to a buffer assumed to be backed by an ASN1_STRING, but not all SANs are backed by ASN1_STRING, so accessing the buffer for such a type can lead to out-of-bounds memory access. This vulnerability is addressed in swift-nio-ssl version 2.37.2.

Affected:
- Apple / swift-nio-ssl: affected 0 <2.37.2 (custom)

- Assigner: apple | Published: 2026-07-23 | Updated: 2026-07-23 | Max CVSS: 7.5
- CWE: When initializing an RSA public key from DER or PEM bytes throws an error, the EVP_PKEY* is double-freed: first in the catch block, then in the deinit. This can lead to a crash on future memory allocations. This double-free manifests when BoringSSL cannot decode the public key from the bytes provided.; CWE-415 CWE-415 Double Free
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.5 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=poc, Automatable=yes, Technical Impact=partial

When initializing an RSA public key from DER or PEM bytes throws an error, the EVP_PKEY* is double-freed: first in the catch block, then in the deinit. This can lead to a crash on future memory allocations. This double-free manifests when BoringSSL cannot decode the public key from the bytes provided. This vulnerability is addressed in swift-crypto version 4.5.1.

Affected:
- Apple / swift-crypto: affected 0 <4.5.1 (custom)

This vulnerability is addressed in container version 1.2.0.

### CVE-2026-113951
- Assigner: apple | Published: 2026-10-23 | Updated: 2026-11-02 | Max CVSS: 7.8
- CWE: If an attacker can write to the filesystem of a container k8s cluster container, they can plant an exec credential plugin in /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf. kubectl will run that plugin as the macOS host user the next time someone pulls the cluster's kubeconfig onto the host with container k8s write-config or create and then runs kubectl against it — turning filesystem access inside an untrusted Linux container into arbitrary command execution on the host.; CWE-276 CWE-276 Incorrect Default Permissions
- CVSS 3.1 (CISA-ADP): 7.8 HIGH `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H`
- SSVC (CISA-ADP): Exploitation=none, Automatable=no, Technical Impact=total

If an attacker can write to the filesystem of a container k8s cluster container, they can plant an exec credential plugin in /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf. kubectl will run that plugin as the macOS host user the next time someone pulls the cluster's kubeconfig onto the host with container k8s write-config or create and then runs kubectl against it — turning filesystem access inside an untrusted Linux container into arbitrary command execution on the host. This vulnerability is addressed in Container version 1.5.0.

Affected:
- Apple / Container: affected 0 <1.5.0 (custom)

References:
- https://github.com/apple/container/security/advisories/GHSA-44v5-vx46-ghv6
